_meta.keyKnowledge: We are learning about what taxation is, why governments collect it, and how it pays for services that benefit everyone.

toLevel2.question: Taxes are payments collected by governments to fund services for the community.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Tax revenue funds public services such as schools, hospitals, and roads.

distractors.explanation: Taxes are not optional donations; they are payments collected by government to pay for shared services.

toLevel2.question: Income tax is paid by businesses only, never by individual workers.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Income tax is paid mainly by individual workers based on what they earn, and also by some businesses.

distractors.explanation: Income tax is mostly a personal tax on earnings; treating it as business-only misses the largest source of income tax revenue.

toLevel2.question: The GST is a tax added to many goods and services bought in Australia.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: GST stands for Goods and Services Tax and is added to most things sold in shops.

distractors.explanation: GST applies broadly to goods and services purchased, which is what makes it different from a tax on income.

toLevel2.question: All money paid in taxes is kept by individual government workers for personal use.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Tax revenue is used to fund public services and is not personal income for government workers.

distractors.explanation: Treating taxes as personal pay for officials confuses public revenue with personal pay.

toLevel2.question: Public schools in Australia are funded mainly through taxes paid by citizens.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Public school funding comes largely from taxation collected by federal and state governments.

distractors.explanation: Most public school costs are met by tax revenue rather than by individual school fees.

toLevel2.question: Public hospitals are funded entirely by patient fees and never receive any tax revenue.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Public hospitals receive most of their funding through tax revenue, not patient fees alone.

distractors.explanation: Treating public hospitals as fee-only ignores the central role of tax revenue in funding public health.

toLevel2.question: Road repairs in most communities are paid for entirely by individual drivers using cash on the spot.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Road repairs are usually funded by tax revenue, not by drivers paying cash directly at the roadside.

distractors.explanation: Treating road costs as paid in cash by passing drivers misses how road funding flows through tax revenue.

toLevel2.question: Public services would receive more funding if no one paid any taxes at all.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Tax revenue is a major funding source, so removing it would reduce funding rather than increase it.

distractors.explanation: Reversing the link between tax revenue and service funding misses how public services depend on tax.

toLevel2.question: Taxes always pay for entirely private goods that only one person can use at a time.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Taxes mainly fund public goods and services that many people share, not private goods used by one person.

distractors.explanation: Public funding is generally directed at shared services rather than items used privately by individuals.

toLevel2.question: A government budget shows where tax revenue is planned to be spent over a period of time.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Budgets set out how a government plans to spend the money it collects through taxes and other sources.

distractors.explanation: A budget is the public document that shows planned spending across services, programs, and other priorities.

toLevel2.question: Different countries have very similar tax rules, with no important differences in what is taxed.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Tax rules differ widely between countries in what is taxed, who pays, and the rates that apply.

distractors.explanation: Treating tax rules as uniform across countries ignores major differences in tax systems internationally.

toLevel2.question: Public services like libraries depend partly on tax revenue to keep operating each year.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Many public services, including local libraries, are funded through a mix of tax revenue and other sources.

distractors.explanation: Removing tax revenue would put many local services at risk because tax is one of their main funding sources.

toLevel2.question: What is taxation?
toLevel2.correct: Money individuals and businesses pay to government to fund services
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Taxation is the system by which governments collect money to fund public services.

distractors.answer: Money the government pays workers as a private bonus each year
distractors.explanation: Taxation is collected from people, not paid to them as a bonus.

distractors.answer: Money charities collect to support local sporting clubs in winter
distractors.explanation: Charity collections are not taxation; tax is collected by government under law.

toLevel2.question: Which one of the following is the main reason governments collect taxes?
toLevel2.correct: To fund public services such as schools, hospitals, and roads
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Tax revenue is used to pay for public services that benefit the community.

distractors.answer: To allow government workers to keep the money for personal use
distractors.explanation: Tax revenue funds services, not personal pay for government workers.

distractors.answer: To replace charity donations made by people each weekend
distractors.explanation: Charity is voluntary and separate from the public funding role of tax.

toLevel2.question: Income tax is collected mainly on which one of the following?
toLevel2.correct: The money workers earn from their jobs
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Income tax is collected mainly on the wages and salaries that people earn from work.

distractors.answer: The clothing every person wears each day
distractors.explanation: Clothing is not the base on which income tax is calculated.

distractors.answer: The buses that operate on public routes
distractors.explanation: Buses are not the base on which income tax is calculated.

toLevel2.question: The GST is added to which one of the following?
toLevel2.correct: Many goods and services sold in Australian shops
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The GST is added to most goods and services sold in Australia at the point of sale.

distractors.answer: Money kept under a mattress at home
distractors.explanation: Money sitting at home is not taxed simply for being there.
Personal letters are not generally taxed when posted between friends.

toLevel2.question: From the list below, which item is most likely paid for by tax revenue?
toLevel2.correct: A new public hospital wing built by a state government
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Public hospitals are funded mainly through tax revenue.

distractors.answer: A small private collection of comic books at home
distractors.explanation: A personal collection at home is not funded by tax revenue.

distractors.answer: A school sports team's privately purchased uniforms
distractors.explanation: Privately purchased team uniforms are not funded by tax.

toLevel2.question: Why would removing all tax revenue create problems for public services?
toLevel2.correct: They would lose a major source of their funding
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Tax revenue is a main source of funding, so removing it would cut a large share of service income.

distractors.answer: They would gain extra funding from new sources
distractors.explanation: Removing tax revenue would not by itself create new funding sources.

distractors.answer: They would continue with no change
distractors.explanation: Public services would not be unaffected by the loss of their main income source.

toLevel2.question: Which item is an example of a public good or service that many people share?
toLevel2.correct: A public road used by many drivers and walkers
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A public road is shared by many people; this is a typical public good.

distractors.answer: A privately owned pair of shoes worn at school
distractors.explanation: A pair of shoes used by one person is a private good, not a public good.

distractors.answer: A privately owned phone used at home
distractors.explanation: A personal phone used by one person at home is a private good, not a public good.

toLevel2.question: A government budget is best described as which one of the following?
toLevel2.correct: A plan that shows how a government will collect and spend money
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A government budget sets out planned spending and revenue across services and programs.

distractors.answer: A weekly grocery list written by an individual household
distractors.explanation: A grocery list is a private household plan, not a public budget.

distractors.answer: A long letter from a school principal to all parents
distractors.explanation: A school letter is communication, not a financial plan for a country or council.

toLevel2.question: Which one of the following best explains why tax systems differ between countries?
toLevel2.correct: Each country chooses what to tax and how to fund its public services
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Each country sets its own rules for tax, including what is taxed and at what rate.

distractors.answer: Every country uses an identical tax system created by one global agency
distractors.explanation: There is no single global agency that sets every country's tax rules.

distractors.answer: Tax systems are decided only by individual workers in each country
distractors.explanation: Tax systems are decided through national laws, not by individual workers alone.

toLevel2.question: Which worker is most likely paid through tax revenue rather than private money?
toLevel2.correct: The salary of a teacher in a public school
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Public school teachers are paid mainly through tax revenue.

distractors.answer: The pocket money a student receives at home
distractors.explanation: Pocket money is from family income, not tax revenue.

distractors.answer: The cost of a private toy bought online
distractors.explanation: A private toy is bought from personal funds, not from tax revenue.

toLevel2.question: Which list contains only services commonly funded by tax revenue in Australia?
toLevel2.correct: Public schools, public hospitals, and public roads
toLevel2.correctExplanation: All three items in the correct list are public services funded mainly through tax revenue.

distractors.answer: A privately owned bicycle, a personal phone, and a private holiday
distractors.explanation: All three items in this list are private goods funded by personal money.

distractors.answer: A school sports kit bought by parents and a backyard pool
distractors.explanation: Both items are funded by personal money, not by tax revenue.

toLevel2.question: Why is it useful to learn how tax revenue is spent?
toLevel2.correct: So citizens can understand how public services are funded and used
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Understanding how tax revenue is spent helps citizens follow public debates about services and priorities.

distractors.answer: So citizens can stop paying tax once they understand the system
distractors.explanation: Tax payment is required by law and is not a matter of individual choice.

distractors.answer: So citizens can replace tax revenue with their own private spending
distractors.explanation: Personal spending cannot replace tax revenue at the scale of public services.

toLevel2.sentence: Money that governments collect from individuals and businesses is called {{blank:1}}, and it is used to fund {{blank:2}} services for the community.

blanks.correctExplanation: This option fits the sentence and matches the topic idea being tested.

distractors.explanation: Donation is a voluntary gift, not the regular collection by government.
Season is a period of competition, not a category of government revenue.

blanks.correctExplanation: This option fits the sentence and matches the topic idea being tested.

distractors.explanation: Private services are funded by individuals, not by tax revenue.
Uniformed describes clothing, not a category of services.

toLevel2.sentence: Income tax is collected on the {{blank:1}} that people earn from their work, while GST is added to most goods and services at the point of {{blank:2}}.

blanks.correctExplanation: This option fits the sentence and matches the topic idea being tested.

distractors.explanation: Uniform is clothing, not what income tax is collected on.
Fixture is a scheduled match, not what income tax is collected on.

blanks.correctExplanation: This option fits the sentence and matches the topic idea being tested.

distractors.explanation: Uniform is clothing, not when GST is added to the price.
Season is a period of competition, not when GST is added to the price.

toLevel3.question: If a country collected no income tax, its public hospitals would still have exactly the same funding.
toLevel3.correct: False
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Income tax is a major funding source for public hospitals, so losing it would reduce their funding.

distractors.explanation: Treating hospital funding as untouched by income tax ignores the role of tax revenue in public health.

toLevel3.question: A road built by a state government is most likely funded mainly through tax revenue.
toLevel3.correct: True
toLevel3.correctExplanation: State roads are typically funded through tax revenue rather than fees paid by individual drivers.

distractors.explanation: Most state-built roads rely on tax revenue rather than direct user payments.

toLevel3.question: Tax revenue can fund only one type of service, so it cannot pay for hospitals and schools together.
toLevel3.correct: False
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Tax revenue funds many services at once, including hospitals, schools, roads, and emergency services.

distractors.explanation: Treating tax as single-use ignores how budgets allocate tax revenue across many public services.

toLevel3.question: A government that lowers taxes without changing anything else will usually have less money to spend on public services.
toLevel3.correct: True
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Lower tax rates typically reduce revenue, which can mean less money for public services.

distractors.explanation: Cutting tax usually cuts revenue unless other sources are increased, so spending on services often falls.

toLevel3.question: Income tax and GST are collected in exactly the same way and from exactly the same source.
toLevel3.correct: False
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Income tax is collected on earnings, while GST is collected at the point of sale on goods and services. They use different methods and sources.

distractors.explanation: Treating these two taxes as identical misses how each is collected from a different base of activity.

toLevel3.question: If everyone paid taxes only when they felt like it, public services would receive a steady, reliable income.
toLevel3.correct: False
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Voluntary tax payments would make revenue unstable, so public services would not receive a steady, reliable income.

distractors.explanation: A tax system that depends on willingness rather than law would produce uneven funding for public services.

toLevel3.question: Comparing tax systems between Australia and another country can show how each country chooses to fund services.
toLevel3.correct: True
toLevel3.correctExplanation: International comparisons reveal different funding choices and priorities across tax systems.

distractors.explanation: Comparing tax systems is a common way to see how different countries fund public services.

toLevel3.question: A government budget that lists expected spending and revenue tells citizens nothing about public priorities.
toLevel3.correct: False
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A government budget reveals public priorities by showing where tax revenue is planned to be spent.

distractors.explanation: Budgets are a key public document for understanding priorities; treating them as uninformative ignores their main purpose.

toLevel3.question: A community has many public schools, public hospitals, and a public library. Which idea best explains how all three are mainly funded?
toLevel3.correct: They are mainly funded by tax revenue collected by government
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Public schools, hospitals, and libraries are typically funded mainly through tax revenue.

distractors.answer: They are mainly funded by personal donations made each weekend
distractors.explanation: Personal donations support some local programs but are not the main source of funding for these services.

distractors.answer: They are mainly funded by international charity organisations
distractors.explanation: Charities support some specific work but are not the main source of funding for public schools, hospitals, and libraries.

toLevel3.question: If a state government decides to lower income tax rates without changing anything else, which outcome is most likely?
toLevel3.correct: The state will collect less revenue and may have less to spend on services
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Lower tax rates typically reduce revenue, which often means less to spend on public services.

distractors.answer: The state will collect more revenue and have more to spend on services
distractors.explanation: Lower rates do not by themselves raise more revenue.

distractors.answer: The state will collect exactly the same amount of revenue as before
distractors.explanation: Lower rates without other changes typically reduce revenue, not leave it unchanged.

toLevel3.question: Which scenario best illustrates a service that depends on tax revenue?
toLevel3.correct: A public hospital that treats patients in an emergency department
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A public hospital is funded mainly through tax revenue.

distractors.answer: A privately owned bookshop that sells used books for cash
distractors.explanation: A private bookshop earns money from sales, not from tax revenue.

distractors.answer: A private piano teacher who charges parents an hourly rate
distractors.explanation: A private music teacher is paid by parents, not through tax revenue.

toLevel3.question: If everyone in a country chose to pay tax only when they felt like it, what would most likely happen?
toLevel3.correct: Tax revenue would become unreliable, and public services would face funding problems
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Voluntary tax would produce unstable revenue, making public services hard to fund consistently.

distractors.answer: Tax revenue would stay the same because most people would still pay regularly
distractors.explanation: Removing the legal requirement would not keep payments steady.

distractors.answer: Tax revenue would rise sharply because optional payments raise more money than required ones
distractors.explanation: Optional tax systems do not raise more money than legally required ones in practice.

toLevel3.question: Which one of the following best illustrates the link between citizens contributing tax and benefits they receive?
toLevel3.correct: A worker pays income tax, and the local public school where their child attends is funded
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Income tax revenue funds many public services, including local public schools.

distractors.answer: A worker hides earnings from the tax office, and public hospitals expand quickly
distractors.explanation: Hiding income reduces tax revenue and is unlikely to support service expansion.

distractors.answer: A worker pays no income tax, and emergency services double their funding
distractors.explanation: Paying no tax reduces revenue rather than doubling funding for services.

toLevel3.question: A government budget shows that 20 per cent of spending will go to public schools. Which idea best describes what this figure represents?
toLevel3.correct: A planned share of revenue to be used for public school services
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Budget shares show how planned spending is divided across services such as public schools.

distractors.answer: A list of every individual student attending public schools that year
distractors.explanation: Budgets show planned spending categories, not lists of individual students.

distractors.answer: A bill that each student must pay before starting school each term
distractors.explanation: Budget shares are not bills paid by students; public schools are funded mainly through tax revenue.

toLevel3.question: Which scenario best shows how the GST works?
toLevel3.correct: A customer buys a coffee for a price that already includes the GST added at the till
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The GST is added to the price of most goods and services at the point of sale.

distractors.answer: A customer pays an extra fee at home each time they make a coffee themselves
distractors.explanation: Making a coffee at home is not a sale, so the GST does not apply in this case.

distractors.answer: A customer pays a yearly bill to the government based on coffees consumed
distractors.explanation: GST is collected at the time of purchase, not as a yearly personal bill.

toLevel3.question: Why do governments use a planned budget for spending tax revenue?
toLevel3.correct: So spending can be matched to public services across the year in a predictable way
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A budget allows planned, predictable allocation of revenue across many services.

distractors.answer: So tax revenue can be transferred to one private worker to manage as they choose
distractors.explanation: Budgets are public plans, not transfers to a single private worker.

distractors.answer: So tax revenue can be hidden from the public until the year has finished
distractors.explanation: Government budgets are public documents, not hidden from citizens.

toLevel3.question: If a country abolished GST without raising any other tax, which outcome is most likely?
toLevel3.correct: Total tax revenue would fall, and some services would face funding pressure
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Abolishing GST without replacing it would reduce total tax revenue and likely affect services.

distractors.answer: Total tax revenue would rise, and most services would expand quickly
distractors.explanation: Removing a tax does not by itself raise revenue.

distractors.answer: Total tax revenue would remain identical, and services would be unchanged
distractors.explanation: Removing a major tax without replacement typically lowers revenue rather than leaving it unchanged.

toLevel3.question: A community public library closes one day a week to save money. Which idea most likely explains the change?
toLevel3.correct: Tax revenue available for the library has fallen short of planned spending
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Reduced tax revenue is a common reason public services such as libraries cut hours.

distractors.answer: Library books have become impossible to find anywhere in the world
distractors.explanation: Books being missing globally is not a likely reason a single library would cut its hours.

distractors.answer: Library staff have all stopped reading books in their own free time
distractors.explanation: Staff reading habits do not determine whether a library opens to the public.

toLevel3.question: Why might one country have a higher rate of GST than another?
toLevel3.correct: Each country chooses tax rates based on its own funding needs and policies
toLevel3.correctExplanation: GST rates differ because each country chooses how it funds public services.

distractors.answer: Every country sets the same GST rate by law each year
distractors.explanation: There is no global rule fixing the same GST rate for every country.

distractors.answer: GST rates are decided only by the largest single business in each country
distractors.explanation: Tax rates are set by national law, not by a single private business.

toLevel3.question: Which one of the following best explains the relationship between income tax rates and government revenue, all else equal?
toLevel3.correct: When income tax rates are lowered, revenue from income tax usually falls
toLevel3.correctExplanation: All else equal, lower income tax rates collect less revenue from each dollar earned.

distractors.answer: When income tax rates are lowered, revenue from income tax usually rises
distractors.explanation: Lower rates do not by themselves raise revenue; in most short-run situations, they lower it.

distractors.answer: Income tax rates do not affect government revenue under any conditions
distractors.explanation: Income tax rates clearly affect government revenue, so dismissing the link is incorrect.

distractors.explanation: Donations are voluntary and are not the main source of funding for these services.

blanks.correctExplanation: This option fits the sentence and matches the topic idea being tested.

distractors.explanation: Uniforms are clothing, not what is funded by taxation.

blanks.correctExplanation: This option fits the sentence and matches the topic idea being tested.

distractors.explanation: Uniforms are clothing, not what citizens have to pay.

blanks.correctExplanation: This option fits the sentence and matches the topic idea being tested.

distractors.explanation: Uniforms are clothing, not what services would lose.
Fixtures are scheduled matches, not what services would lose.

toLevel4.question: If a council loses tax revenue from rates, its planned spending on parks and libraries is likely to be reduced.
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Lower revenue typically means less money available for council services such as parks and libraries.

distractors.explanation: Council services are funded mainly through rates and other tax revenue, so a loss of revenue normally reduces spending.

toLevel4.question: A small business pays GST on its sales but says taxes have no effect on the prices it charges customers.
toLevel4.correctExplanation: GST is added to the prices customers pay, so taxes do affect the final prices charged at point of sale.

distractors.explanation: Saying GST does not affect prices misses how the tax is added to the final price paid by the customer.

toLevel4.question: Mia notices that her local public school received a new computer lab funded by a state grant. Which idea best explains the funding source?
toLevel4.correct: Tax revenue allocated to public schools through a state government grant
toLevel4.correctExplanation: State grants for public school equipment are funded mainly through tax revenue.

distractors.answer: Personal donations made by computer companies free of charge
distractors.explanation: Companies sometimes donate, but state grants are funded through tax revenue.

distractors.answer: International charity organisations focused only on private schools
distractors.explanation: International charities rarely fund routine public school equipment in Australia.

toLevel4.question: Jarrah's town wants to build a new public library. Which one of the following is the most likely main funding source?
toLevel4.correct: Tax revenue collected by local or state government
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Public libraries are typically funded mainly through tax revenue collected by government.

distractors.answer: Pocket money paid by every child in the town
distractors.explanation: Pocket money is private spending and is not used to fund public buildings.

distractors.answer: Money donated by international charities focused on libraries
distractors.explanation: International charity is not the typical main funder of an Australian public library.

toLevel4.question: Anika sees a road repair sign in her suburb. Which idea best explains where the money for the repairs likely comes from?
toLevel4.correct: From tax revenue used by government to maintain roads in the suburb
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Most road repairs are funded through tax revenue used by government.

distractors.answer: From a private collection passed around the suburb each weekend
distractors.explanation: Private collections do not typically fund suburban road repairs.

distractors.answer: From private fees charged at the spot to drivers using the road
distractors.explanation: Drivers do not usually pay direct on-the-spot fees for road repairs as they pass.

toLevel4.question: Sam reads that government revenue from income tax has fallen. Which outcome is most likely if no other change is made?
toLevel4.correct: The government will have less to spend on public services that depend on income tax
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Lower income tax revenue typically means less to spend on services, all else equal.

distractors.answer: The government will have more to spend on every public service across the country
distractors.explanation: Falling revenue does not increase spending capacity.

distractors.answer: Public services will receive exactly the same level of funding as before
distractors.explanation: Falling revenue without other changes generally reduces, rather than leaves unchanged, service spending.

toLevel4.question: Lila buys a bottle of juice and sees that the price already includes the GST. Which idea best describes what is happening?
toLevel4.correct: The GST has been added to the price as a tax on the sale of goods
toLevel4.correctExplanation: The GST is added to the price of most goods and services at the point of sale.

distractors.answer: The GST has been deducted from the price as a refund to the buyer
distractors.explanation: GST is added to the price, not refunded to the buyer.

distractors.answer: The GST has been transferred to the buyer's bank account at sale
distractors.explanation: GST is collected from the seller, not transferred to the buyer's bank.

toLevel4.question: Kofi compares Australia with another country and finds different tax systems. Which idea best explains why the systems differ?
toLevel4.correct: Each country sets its own tax laws to fund the services it provides
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Tax laws are set nationally, so different countries make different choices.

distractors.answer: Every country uses identical tax laws set by one global office
distractors.explanation: There is no single global office that sets identical tax laws everywhere.

distractors.answer: Tax laws are decided only by individual workers in each country
distractors.explanation: Tax laws are set through national legal processes, not by individual workers alone.

toLevel4.question: Yen reads a budget summary showing 30 per cent of spending will go to public hospitals. Which idea best describes this figure?
toLevel4.correct: A planned share of revenue to be used for public hospital services
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Budget shares show planned spending on services such as public hospitals.

distractors.answer: A list of every patient who will be admitted to hospital that year
distractors.explanation: Budgets list spending categories, not individual patients.

distractors.answer: A fee that every hospital patient will pay before being seen
distractors.explanation: Budget shares are not bills paid by patients; public hospital care is funded mainly through tax.

toLevel4.question: Rosa sees a news report that road repairs in her town will be delayed because of lower tax revenue. Which idea best explains the link?
toLevel4.correct: Lower tax revenue reduces the funds available for council road work
